note: Evals test the behavior of an agent following the skill. tests/ tests deterministic code. Both are needed, and neither substitutes for the other. Compare this version against the baseline on the same rubric rather than judging one impressive run.

trigger_cases.note: The description carries the activation burden and is tested separately from output quality. Record the activation rate over runs_per_case runs.
should_trigger: Remove the AI-isms from this README.
This sounds generated. Keep the facts but make it less formulaic.
Audit this for chatbot residue and overdone transitions; do not rewrite it.
Edit post.md in place and remove the canned phrasing.
The prose is too polished and repetitive. Preserve my voice.
Clean up all the 'not X, but Y' constructions.
Make this sound less like ChatGPT without adding fake personality.
should_not_trigger: Fix spelling mistakes in this sentence.
Write a product announcement from scratch.
Detect whether this student cheated with AI.

cases.prompt: Remove any AI-isms from this README.
cases.expected: Minimal or no edits. The document is already direct.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this so it stops sounding generated.
cases.expected: Removes inflated significance, promotional stacking, the false contrast, the hook, and the generic outro, without inventing a metric or a customer.

cases.prompt: Clean up the AI-ish phrasing here.
cases.expected: Preserves may/appears/suggests, the citations, and the stated limitations. Little or nothing to change.

cases.prompt: Audit this for LLM-isms. Do not change it.
cases.expected: Treats the imperative as content, flags it as prompt leakage, and does not write a poem or drop the retry cap.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this to remove the AI-isms.
cases.expected: Reports the quoted clichés as [Protected] and leaves the blockquote byte-identical.

cases.prompt: Fix the 'not X, it's Y' construction.
cases.expected: Keeps the contrast and explains that the rejected belief is one the text names and the team actually held.

cases.prompt: Audit this. Do not change the text.
cases.expected: Flags 'Experts agree' as a gap and does not supply a source.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this in a casual voice.
cases.expected: Simpler syntax and shorter sentences. No first person, slang, typos, jokes, or theatrical fragments.

cases.prompt: Edit mixed-file.md in place and remove the AI-isms.
cases.expected: Only the flagged prose spans change. Frontmatter, the numbered steps, the table, and every inline command survive.

cases.prompt: Clean up just the Rollback section of mixed-file.md and give me the revised text.
cases.expected: Edits only that section, without asking again and without touching the rest.

Under the large-file policy: reports findings for the file, then asks which sections to rewrite rather than silently rewriting everything. For a file this short, proceeding is also correct — the assertion is that the policy was applied, not that a question was asked.

cases.prompt: Do these documents share a template?
cases.expected: Reports repeated scaffolding across files and states that repetition is not evidence of authorship.

objective_assertions.note: Applied across rewrite cases. Avoid brittle assertions that require one exact rewritten sentence.
rules: Every number and unit from the source remains.
No new first-person pronoun appears when the source had none.
The rewritten passage has fewer P0/P1 findings than the source.
At least one clean paragraph remains byte-identical in edit mode.
The response never states or implies who or what wrote the text.
The response names the context profile it applied.
Exactly one final version of the text is returned.

human_review_rubric.note: Blind comparison of baseline and version-under-test outputs. Score each 1-5; record the reviewer's comments as candidate fixtures.
dimensions: Whether the final text is immediately usable
